contract.reader: A C programmer with basic digital logic and no embedded experience, deciding whether and where to start the series
contract.problem: Knowing what the five entries cover, why in this order, what is out of scope and which conventions they share
contract.outcome: Know the prerequisites and scope (single-core microcontrollers); follow the sequence as a chain of limits removed (superloop, interrupts and DMA, buses, RTOS, measurement); know the code, platform and unit conventions; have four assessable objectives
contract.contribution: The order is explained as each entry removing a limit of the one before, ending with measurement checking the analysis
contract.evidence: The five entries; the sequence, scope and convention statements were checked against them in the live review
contract.limitations: An overview; total reading time not stated

findings.location: Entries list, cards 2 to 5 (desktop-light-02 and 03, mobile-light-05 and 06)
findings.problem: The descriptions of entries 2 to 5 are 'How ...' fragments, not sentences, unlike card 1; card 2 ends with the unexpanded abbreviation ISR
findings.whyItMatters: Standards 8.1 asks for one complete sentence; the same text is each entry's meta description and RSS summary
findings.action: Rewrite the four descriptions as 70-165 character sentences through each entry's review stages and update the Vietnamese descriptions in the same commit
findings.acceptance: On new captures every entry card shows a one-sentence description and card 2 uses no unexpanded abbreviation other than DMA

history.note: live review: accepted-with-follow-up (editorial/live-reviews/series/embedded-and-real-time-systems.md); library decision: retain
